policy.scope: source-bound canonical MIR legality, exact simplification, bounds/fact derivation, loop/vector representation, reduction, acceleration, and cost rejection
policy.foreign_suffix: target ABI, foreign libraries, runtime resources, scheduler, and finite workload measurements remain explicit downstream boundaries

claim.statement: Each production canonical MIR optimization pass is joined to the shared lowering operation denominator and carries a conditional preservation certificate. Legality is checked before profitability; scalar, vector, parallel, and layout choices retain the same numerical, failure, mutation, input, cleanup, and schedule contract. The certificate is not a universal semantic or performance proof.
preconditions: The #2898/#2919 canonical operation denominator is read from the generated compiler obligation relation; this stage adds no second optimizer or denominator.

Canonical MIR legality, exact folding, CFG, bounds, purity, loop, vector, reduction, acceleration, and ordering facts are produced by crates/jet-foundation/src/MIROptimization.rs and its existing acceleration module.
A transform runs only when its semantic premises hold; an expert rejection or a cost-model rejection uses the same canonical implementation and cannot legalize an illegal transform.
Source identity, IR identity, target/layout identity, failure order, numerical rules, alias premises, and observation order remain explicit across composition.
Unknown compiler observations, unavailable targets, and foreign suffixes remain unverified rather than proved.
unsupported_cases: A missing, stale, or unbound production optimization pass certificate
A source/IR/target identity mismatch or a certificate attached to a different operation
Reordered effects or failures, extra input consumption, invalid alias assumptions, unchecked arithmetic reassociation, or dropped cleanup
A cost or workload selection used to make an illegal transform legal
A universal claim that scalar, vector, parallel, layout, or acceleration is profitable on every target or workload
A fresh compiler replay or behavioral qualification when the pinned compiler is unavailable

execution.crash_policy: tool failures, unavailable binaries, and malformed responses are unavailable or invalid_oracle, never preservation

binding_methods.implementation: the single canonical MIR optimizer, legality verifier, exact transformations, fact derivation, and canonical order
binding_methods.construction: source-bound optimization relation with exact implementation symbol, origin, premises, observations, target contract, and rejection route
binding_methods.limit: construction binding is not a universal preservation or profitability theorem

binding_methods.implementation: canonical MIR operation/terminator/fact types and the D-ACCEL1 legality-plus-cost gate
binding_methods.candidate_binding: current source SHA-256, compiler-proof identity, target/configuration descriptors
binding_methods.limit: no compiler, Jet, target, scheduler, or workload execution is performed by this source checker

binding_methods.certificate: every generated production pass, legal/invalid source witness, composition premise, negative control, and optional canonical TIR/MIR route observation
binding_methods.limit: finite route observations remain proof-blocking until an independently derived semantic goal has a pinned formal discharge and cost remains separate

selection: canonical TExprKind and TStmt operation rows
#2898.rule: reuse the generated operation denominator; do not add an optimizer-specific semantic engine

#2919.rule: bind every production pass to the current MIROptimization implementation route

coverage.qualification_rule: A boundary remains blocked unless every current production optimization pass has a current source binding, complete premises, and matched canonical route observations; no finite route observation is promoted to semantic legality, profitability, or proof without an independent formal discharge.

implementation_route.decision_route: Legality facts and rejection reasons are established by the canonical MIR optimizer before any D-ACCEL1 or workload-cost decision. Scalar, vector, parallel, and layout are target facts, not alternate semantic engines.
implementation_route.single_route_rule: No adapter-specific optimizer or semantic evaluator is introduced; all targets consume the canonical checked MIR and its preserved failure/order/layout facts.

proven: The checker joins the exact generated canonical operation relation to the current #2939 optimization boundary.
Every registered production optimization pass requires implementation identity, origin identity, side conditions, all observations, target choices, and separate legality/profitability fields.
Forged, reordered, over-consuming, aliased, unsound, cost-overriding, and wrong-operation certificates are rejected structurally.
Composition requires the ordered pass relation and preserves observations, origin, side conditions, legality, profitability, and target representation.
assumed: D-TIER-ONEIR1, D-COMPILER-PROOF1, D-ACCEL1, I3, and I9 define the shared checked MIR route and acceleration gate.
#2898 supplies the canonical operation denominator and #2919 supplies the current integrated implementation route.
Foreign compiler, target ABI/layout, allocator/resource schedule, scheduler, and external callback environments satisfy their named contracts.
tested: Legal and deliberately invalid witness sources are source-hash bound and kept distinct without executing them.
Source/IR/target identity checks, premise retention, legality-before-profitability separation, and negative-control mutation sensitivity are present in the checker.
blocked: Universal preservation for all source programs, MIR states, target layouts, failures, effects, schedules, and resource bounds.
Fresh compiler execution, replay of AOT/JIT/interpreter/check observations, and qualification of profitability or foreign behavior.
A generated operation row with stale source identity or missing observation evidence.
